quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
In the middle between both.

questions.explanation: Steer down the middle between the oncoming cars and the parked cars.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other car.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to the right lane when you see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror. This means you have enough space between you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
You will always have to stop at the upcoming railroad crossing.
You should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming. Slow down, look and listen, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Go through without stopping.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.explanation: Police officers directing traffic override all traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: When parallel parking on a downhill slope, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them away from the curb.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter the road, what should you do at the sidewalk?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are walking.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: Always stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps avoid crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.explanation: Never count on other drivers giving you the right-of-way. Always yield when it prevents a collision.

questions.question: You must give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether in a marked crosswalk or not. For safety, give pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes and shift into neutral.

questions.explanation: If your rear end skids left, steer left. Take your foot off the brake. Steer toward where you want the front of the car to go. This straightens out your vehicle.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Drive off the road.
Use a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic in the nearest lane. Match your speed to traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch for other cars and do not expect them to make room for you.

questions.question: When driving at high speeds, signal ____ before you turn.

options.text: Two seconds
Four to five seconds
10 seconds

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before changing lanes or turning. At high speeds, signal four to five seconds before moving left or right.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstates, if you are driving slower than traffic, use the right lane.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.
The road ahead has sharp turns or curves.
Heavy traffic is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that wet pavement is slippery. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic comes from both directions.
You are near a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves in both directions.

questions.question: When you prepare to turn left from a two-way street, drive:

options.text: Near the right edge of the road.
Near the centerline.
Left of the centerline.

questions.explanation: To turn left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press the brakes gently.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, do not use the brakes. Steer to regain control until the car moves safely again.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move far to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke blocks the road, slow down right away. Drive as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or worse.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not count on the other driver to make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not count on the other driver to make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume the space is free or that other drivers will give you the right-of-way.

questions.question: Drivers should use high beam headlights:

options.text: When no vehicles are coming toward you.
When there may be people walking near the road.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: High beams let you see twice as far as low beams. Use them on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas, or where people may be walking. Only use high beams when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: If you cannot see a gap in traffic to enter the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you cannot see a gap in traffic, slow down on the ramp to wait for one. Do not stop at the end of the ramp. You need space to speed up and match the freeway traffic before you enter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Road curves ahead.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means you must stop.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from headlights of a car coming toward you?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the road's centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright headlights. Then look back ahead to see where the other car is.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice, what should drivers with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Do not use the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and then:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the right edge of the road. If the brakes fail, the car will roll away from the road instead of into traffic.
